intro_script: Welcome to your daily dose of robotics and automation news from July 18th, 2026. We've got updates on new open AI tools, automotive AI partnerships, and physical AI advancements across the industry. Tune in now.
outro_script: And that's all for today's dose of the automated world! May your algorithms run smoothly. Until tomorrow, keep building brilliantly. Thanks for tuning in to Robotics Rundown!

items.title: Nvidia and Hugging Face expand LeRobot with new open robotics AI tools
items.summary: Nvidia and Hugging Face expanded their collaboration to integrate new AI models and frameworks into the open-source LeRobot platform. This expansion includes integrating Nvidia Isaac GR00T 1.7, a vision-language-action foundation model, and the Isaac Teleop framework. These additions aim to provide developers with a standardized workflow for collecting data, training, and deploying AI-powered robots. Future plans involve integrating Nvidia Cosmos 3 to allow for generating synthetic robotics data and simulations. The partnership seeks to broaden access to physical AI technologies by combining their respective developer communities.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Nvidia and Hugging Face expand LeRobot with new open robotics AI tools. This report details the integration of new artificial intelligence models and frameworks into the open-source LeRobot platform. The collaboration involved incorporating Nvidia Isaac GR00T 1.7, a vision-language-action foundation model, alongside the Isaac Teleop framework into the existing system. This expansion establishes a standardized workflow for developers engaged in collecting data, training, and deploying artificial intelligence on robotic systems. Future developments are scheduled to integrate Nvidia Cosmos 3 for generating synthetic robotics data and simulations within the platform. This partnership aims to increase accessibility to physical artificial intelligence technologies across developer communities. The integration signals a move toward more accessible methods for robotics development and simulation.

items.title: Toyota and Nvidia expand partnership to develop AI for vehicles, factories and cities
items.summary: Toyota and Nvidia expanded their partnership to develop physical AI technologies for vehicles, factories, and cities. This collaboration involves deploying Nvidia's computing, AI software, and simulation technologies across Toyota's business areas. Specific applications include advanced driver-assistance systems, AI-assisted software engineering using Nvidia models, and factory simulations with Omniverse and Isaac Sim. Furthermore, the partnership includes using multimodal vision-language models for urban traffic analysis in mobility systems. The goal is to create an AI infrastructure for more autonomous vehicles, intelligent manufacturing, and responsive urban environments.

This effort aims to establish an AI infrastructure supporting autonomous vehicles, intelligent manufacturing, and responsive urban environments. The development signals a tangible integration of advanced computing into real-world industrial and transportation systems.

items.summary: Fujitsu is partnering with Fanuc, Yaskawa, and Kawasaki to develop physical AI using Nvidia technology across manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare. This collaboration aims to create a collaborative control platform connecting digital systems with robots and physical equipment. The initiative seeks to address challenges like labor shortages and aging workforces through physical AI adoption. They plan to develop an open, sovereign platform integrating AI, robotics, simulation, and data analysis for interoperability and security. The project will utilize Nvidia tools to accelerate robot learning and simulation workflows.

items.title: Kimi K3 launch shifts AI frontier focus
items.summary: The Kimi K3 launch sparked a reassessment of how close Chinese open-weight models are to the AI frontier, pressuring US labs to accelerate. The focus shifted from raw compute to efficiency stacks like MoE routing and data curation as determinants of capability. Benchmarks show Kimi K3 performs strongly in coding agents and frontend tasks, surpassing some Western models in specific areas. Technical innovations like Kimi Delta Attention suggest significant gains in speed and cost for long context processing. The value is increasingly shifting toward orchestration, memory systems, and workflows rather than just base model access.
items.audio_script: From latent.space, Kimi K3 launch shifts AI frontier focus. This report details how the release of the Kimi K3 model prompted a reassessment of the current state of open-weight models relative to the AI frontier, emphasizing efficiency stacks as key determinants of capability. The launch instigated a shift in focus from raw computational power to advanced techniques such as Mixture of Experts routing and data curation methods as critical factors determining performance. Benchmarks indicate that Kimi K3 demonstrates strong performance in coding agents and frontend tasks, achieving results superior to some Western models in these specific domains. Technical advancements, including the introduction of Kimi Delta Attention, suggest substantial improvements in the speed and cost associated with processing long context. The resulting value is increasingly concentrated on orchestration systems, memory management, and workflow design rather than solely base model access. This development signals an industry trend toward prioritizing efficiency and system integration in future large language model development.

items.title: Weave Robotics launches Isaac, its first mobile humanoid robot
items.summary: Weave Robotics has introduced Isaac 1, a wheeled, home humanoid designed for everyday chores like folding laundry and tidying rooms. Priced at $7,999 or a monthly subscription, the robot features a friendly appearance with soft fabric and adjustable height. Isaac 1 possesses autonomous navigation to move between rooms and can be controlled remotely via an app. It is equipped with an eight-hour battery and privacy shutters for its cameras while working or charging. The robot is positioned as an affordable entry point into home robotics, building upon the lessons learned from its predecessor, Isaac 0.

The robot is priced at seven thousand nine hundred ninety-nine dollars or offered through a monthly subscription and features a friendly appearance with soft fabric and adjustable height. Isaac 1 utilizes autonomous navigation to move between rooms and allows for remote control through an application. It is equipped with an eight-hour battery life and privacy shutters for its cameras during operation or charging, establishing itself as an accessible entry point into home robotics. This development indicates continued progression in the field of domestic automation and mobile robotics research.

items.title: mimic Robotics unveils full-stack platform for dexterous robot manipulation
items.summary: mimic Robotics introduced a full-stack platform featuring the mimic hand M1, a tendon-driven robotic hand, and the mimic wearable U1 exoskeleton. This system aims to advance general-purpose dexterous manipulation for industrial robots by addressing challenges in collecting high-quality AI training data. The design keeps the human hand morphology constant across hardware, data collection, and model training to eliminate cross-embodiment gaps. The mimic hand M1 offers 15 degrees of freedom with force sensing and supports payloads over 25 kg. Furthermore, the platform includes custom middleware to reduce latency for faster AI inference and reliable robot control.

The platform includes the mimic hand M1, a tendon-driven robotic hand, and the mimic wearable U1 exoskeleton. The design maintains consistent human hand morphology across the hardware, data collection, and model training to mitigate cross-embodiment gaps. The mimic hand M1 provides fifteen degrees of freedom along with force sensing and is capable of supporting payloads exceeding twenty-five kilograms. This development signals a potential advancement in creating more realistic and robust training scenarios for advanced robotic systems.

items.title: The Download: perimenopause misinformation and China’s latest AI leap
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: Hype surrounding perimenopause is often fueled by misinformation, as there are no definitive tests for it and treatment suggestions often lack scientific evidence. Not all midlife symptoms are hormonal, and the conversation is increasingly shaped by inaccurate information. Concurrently, China has advanced its AI capabilities by releasing the world's largest open AI model, intensifying competition with US models like OpenAI. Other technological advancements include potential life on nearby exoplanets and breakthroughs in brain-machine interfaces. Furthermore, new technologies are being explored to transform human waste into agricultural resources.
items.audio_script: From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "The Download: perimenopause misinformation and China’s latest AI leap". The discussion centers on the lack of definitive testing for perimenopause and the dissemination of unsubstantiated treatment advice as the conversation is increasingly shaped by inaccurate information. Concurrently, China has released the world's largest open AI model, intensifying the global competition with models developed by organizations such as OpenAI. The pace of AI development continues to reshape the technological landscape.

items.title: Agility Robotics opens new Fremont facility to accelerate physical AI development
items.summary: Agility Robotics opened a 60,000-square-foot facility in Fremont, California, to accelerate physical AI development for customer operations. This new site will serve as the software and capabilities hub for training and testing AI technologies that enhance the skills of their humanoid robot, Digit. The location places Agility's development in the heart of Silicon Valley, capitalizing on its leading AI talent. The facility will house nearly 200 employees from various engineering and operations teams driving AI innovation for enterprise applications. This expansion supports growing demand for humanoid robots in warehouses and manufacturing by improving safety and productivity.

items.title: With new funding, Monumental plans to bring its construction robots to the U.S.
items.summary: Monumental raised $32 million in Series B funding to expand its construction robotics into the U.S. The financing will support growing the engineering team, launching in the U.S., and increasing robot deployment across Europe. The robots use advanced sensors and AI software to autonomously lay bricks with millimeter precision on construction sites. Monumental aims to alleviate labor shortages by handling repetitive masonry work, allowing skilled workers to focus on higher-value tasks. The company emphasizes that human operators remain essential for overseeing the entire construction process safely.

This financing will be utilized to grow the engineering team, facilitate the launch in the U.S., and increase robot deployment across Europe. The robots operate by employing advanced sensors and artificial intelligence software to autonomously lay bricks on construction sites with millimeter precision. Human operators are maintained as essential components for overseeing the entire construction procedure safely. items.title: McLaren Construction to deploy autonomous robots at scale in partnership with FieldAI
items.summary: McLaren Construction partnered with FieldAI to deploy autonomous quadruped robots on UK construction sites. These robots will capture imagery, generate point cloud data, and support progress verification and deviation analysis against design models. This technology aims to ensure correct installation at delivery, improving quality control and reducing rework. The partnership leverages FieldAI's Field Foundation Models for robots capable of adapting to complex, unstructured environments. This deployment supports McLaren's broader digital transformation strategy by enhancing productivity, safety, and quality assurance on site.

Strider develops autonomous quadruped robots supported by an AI-powered, hardware-agnostic software platform for various industrial tasks. These robots are designed for applications like infrastructure inspection, mining, and asset monitoring in challenging environments. The company aims to establish India as a leader in intelligent legged robotic systems for industrial and defense uses.

items.title: Robbyant releases LingBot-World 2.0 with hour-long real-time world generation
items.summary: Robbyant released LingBot-World 2.0, an open-sourced interactive world model with support for hour-long real-time generation. This update significantly extends stable world generation from minutes to continuous sessions while maintaining high visual quality. The system produces 720p video at 60 frames per second and allows real-time user interaction via the Reactor platform. LingBot-World 2.0 utilizes a dual-agent architecture, featuring a Pilot Agent and a Director Agent, for dynamic world evolution. Internal testing confirmed stable visual fidelity during long generation sessions and supports multi-user collaboration.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Robbyant releases LingBot-World 2.0 with hour-long real-time world generation. The update extends stable world generation from minutes to continuous sessions through a dual-agent architecture incorporating a Pilot Agent and a Director Agent designed for dynamic world evolution. Internal testing confirmed stable visual fidelity during these extended generation sessions, producing 720p video at sixty frames per second and enabling real-time user interaction via the Reactor platform, supporting multi-user collaboration. This advancement demonstrates significant progress in creating sustained, high-fidelity simulated environments with advanced artificial intelligence systems.

items.summary: Deise Yumi Asami, founder of Maximo, discusses how AI-enabled robotics is transforming solar construction. Her platform automates the installation of solar modules using AI-based vision for increased speed and efficiency. Maximo leverages robotics, AI vision, and smart field deployment to reshape renewable energy infrastructure. As a result, robotic automation makes solar panel installation faster, safer, and more efficient. Asami's work is supported by her extensive experience in developing energy solutions at AES.

items.title: Luyten opens early reservations for Ascend A27 automated construction platform
items.summary: Luyten has opened early reservations for its Ascend A27 automated construction platform following its global launch. Early reservers will receive priority production allocation and an introductory offer, with deposits credited to the final price. The Ascend A27 converts conventional tower cranes into robotic systems capable of automated large-scale 3D concrete printing. This platform integrates robotics, AI, and digital manufacturing to automate construction while utilizing existing crane infrastructure. Early reservation customers will be part of the first commercial deployment group for the system.

items.title: This Graduate Student Equips NASA’s Robots With Assembly Skills
items.summary: A graduate student named Sarah Downs developed an algorithm for robotic assembly in space. This work was done in collaboration with NASA and the U.S. Air Force. The algorithm allows robots to install antennas on satellites by inserting them into the correct positions. This advancement equips NASA's robots with necessary assembly skills.

The work involved a collaboration between a graduate student and NASA and the U.S. Air Force to create this novel algorithm for robotic assembly procedures. The methodology focused on developing the computational framework that guides the robotic systems through the complex process of antenna installation, ensuring precise placement required for satellite functionality. items.summary: Automation investment success hinges on the software layer, with Warehouse Execution Systems acting as the crucial "brain" connecting robotics and equipment. Software-first strategies provide the necessary flexibility to evolve operations without being locked into rigid hardware. Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) are becoming core infrastructure supported by accessible models like Robotics-as-a-Service, proving their scalability. AI enables predictive operations through real-time insights, which requires a strong orchestration platform across all systems. Future success will depend on treating automation as a flexible growth platform built on adaptable software foundations.

items.title: Interview with Scott Zerkle of Panasonic Connect: ‘AI is only as good as the data it receives’
items.summary: AI's greatest current value in electronics manufacturing is predictive maintenance and defect detection, not replacing workers. The next major step involves connecting data across machines, materials, and processes to enable factories that continuously learn from production history. Component miniaturization demands extreme precision in printing and placement, pushing for real-time correction during production runs. Automation helps ensure consistency by monitoring the 5Ms (human, machine, material, method, measurement) to catch deviations before they become defects. The future lies in the convergence of AI, sensing, and automation creating interconnected manufacturing ecosystems.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Scott Zerkle of Panasonic Connect: ‘AI is only as good as the data it receives’". This report details the current application and future trajectory of artificial intelligence within electronics manufacturing, emphasizing that AI's present value lies in predictive maintenance and defect detection rather than workforce replacement. The next significant development involves integrating data across machines, materials, and processes to establish factories capable of continuous learning from production history. Component miniaturization necessitates extreme precision in printing and placement, driving the need for real-time correction during manufacturing runs. Automation supports consistency by monitoring the five Ms: human, machine, material, method, and measurement, allowing for deviation detection prior to defect formation. The future points toward an interconnected ecosystem built upon the convergence of AI, sensing, and automation. This shift indicates a focus on creating deeply integrated, self-optimizing manufacturing environments moving forward.

items.title: Aetina adds support for Nvidia Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules
items.summary: Aetina plans to expand its Nvidia Jetson Thor-based systems by supporting the new Jetson T3000 and T2000 AI modules for robotics and industrial edge AI. These support options will be integrated into Aetina's upcoming DeviceEdge AIE-KT (fan-based) and AIE-PT (fanless) platforms. The Jetson T3000 module offers up to 865 FP4 TFLOPS, while the T2000 offers up to 400 FP4 TFLOPS, targeting various AI agent applications. Aetina will use these modules to scale robotics projects from development through production deployments. Nvidia anticipates these modules will be available in the first quarter of 2027 and support the Nvidia AI software ecosystem.

items.title: Smart glasses are deeply creepy. Why are celebrities like Kylie Jenner endorsing them?
items.summary: Smart glasses raise significant privacy and safety concerns due to their surveillance capabilities. Concerns are particularly acute for women regarding non-consensual filming, including sexual abuse, by others. While Meta claims safety features like LED lights and tamper detection, these measures have been circumvented by some users. Face-recognition technology is embedded within the AI app, creating potential for government or stalker misuse of biometric data. Celebrities are being used to endorse these products, which further normalizes the issue despite widespread backlash.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Smart glasses are deeply creepy. Why are celebrities like Kylie Jenner endorsing them?". This report examines the privacy and safety concerns surrounding smart glasses and the use of celebrity endorsements in the technology sector. Smart glasses introduce significant privacy and safety issues due to their inherent surveillance capabilities, raising particular concerns for women regarding non-consensual filming. While companies such as Meta have implemented safety features including LED lights and tamper detection, reports indicate these measures have been bypassed by some users. Face recognition technology integrated within the applications creates potential avenues for the misuse of biometric data by governmental or stalking entities. The endorsement strategy utilized by celebrities serves to normalize these concerns despite existing public backlash against the technology. The industry must address the integration of biometric surveillance and user consent protocols immediately.

items.title: Fragrance clubs create new social connections
items.summary: Fragrance clubs are emerging as a new form of social connection, transforming the solitary experience of scent into a collective activity. These clubs take many forms, including blind-sniff meetups, workshops, and fragrance swaps across various cities. The trend is fueled by the growth of the fragrance industry and a desire among people for in-person socialization. These clubs foster meaningful conversations centered on personal feelings and memories rather than technical jargon. They are likened to book or wine clubs due to their lower barrier to entry and focus on shared emotional experiences.
